executionPlan: Read constitution, insights, stage contract, game-dev report, design sections 3.1/5.3/8/9. Ran lint, test and build on Node 22 in the worktree. Diffed 710f034..f8da3ab (name filter for the section 9 list, TalkingAvatar diff read in full, em dash and machine-path greps). Browser: the Playwright MCP tools can only tap keys (keydown+keyup in the same call), so the avatar never moved from them. Fell back to Bash: headless system Chrome via DevTools protocol (software GL) against the already-running dev server on port 3100, with real held keys, CDP screenshots and a read-only scene probe (position of the avatar root read from the three scene). Quantified speeds, step/ramp/wall/pit/jump behaviour from position traces. Reproduced the ramp-45 defect in a throwaway Rapier probe test (created and deleted, git status clean), and confirmed the unit test assertion is vacuous.
summary: REJECTED. Gates are green and match the dev claims (lint 0, 65 tests in 5 files, build 0, / First Load JS 125 kB). Diff scope is clean. The browser gate passes for Play/Exit, WASD, run, jump, camera drag, R, wall, 0.2 m step, 0.35 m step, 30 degree ramp and pit respawn. It FAILS for the 45 degree ramp: the avatar climbs it (feet y reaches 4.24 m) in the browser at both walk and run speed. Reproduced in real Rapier under Node when the capsule starts about 1 m from the ramp (peak 3.13 walking, 4.25 running). The dev's unit test only passes because it starts 2 m away and asserts the end feet height after 5 s, which is also satisfied if the avatar climbs and steps off the top. The criterion requires the 45 degree ramp to block, so the verdict is rejected. Walk and run speeds measured 1.57 and 3.75 m/s, acceptable for the prototype. Mobile and real-GPU checks were not done (out of scope for this gate).

Run from the side: q-run-side-1.png to q-run-side-4.png show a forward lean, facing the travel direction, not sideways; limbs are not stretched. Walk from behind: q-walk-behind-t1.png, q-walk-behind-t2.png. Run from behind: A-run-behind.png. findings.trigger: Approach the 45 degree ramp (TEST_ARENA ramp-45, x -7) from roughly 1 m before its low end (z about 1) and hold W, with or without Shift.
findings.consequence: The avatar climbs the 45 degree ramp to its top (feet y 4.24 m) even though maxSlopeDeg is 40, so the M1 collision requirement (45 degree ramp blocks) is not met, and the unit test hides it. Likely cause, not proven: Rapier's autostep or the STEP_PROBE accept path steps up the 0.5 m thick ramp edge and then follows it; I did not bisect which.

findings.rule: Spec M1 acceptance (45 degree ramp blocks) and the stage criterion; code-review checklist: behaviour must match the acceptance criterion

findings.trigger: Run npm test: the test 'climbs a 30 degree ramp and is blocked by a 45 degree ramp' passes while the 45 degree ramp is climbable.
findings.consequence: The assertion for the 45 degree ramp is vacuous: it starts 2 m from the ramp (z=0) and checks only feetY < 0.5 after 5 s, which is also true if the avatar climbs and steps off the top. The start position also never reaches the failing case. The regression gate gives false assurance. Fix suggestion: start at z about 1 and assert the peak feet height during the whole run (not the final), for both walk and run, and after fixing F1 confirm by reverting the guard that the test goes red.
findings.evidence: Source lines 208-212 (rig at z 0, run(b,5,fwd(true)), expect(feetY) < 0.5). Probe with z0=0 gives peak 0.00 (passes), z0=1.1 gives peak 3.13/4.25.
findings.rule: testing skill: assert the behaviour, not the end state; a probe or test never seen to fail is not evidence

assumptions: The Playwright MCP tool set available to me can only tap keys (type/click), so it could not hold keys; I used headless system Chrome driven over the DevTools protocol (software GL) for held keys, against the dev server on port 3100, and I record this plainly. No other server was started and port 3000 was not touched.
Positions were read from the three.js scene (root group above the first SkinnedMesh) via an injected read-only script; this is test instrumentation, not part of the product.
Frame rate under software GL was about 27 rAF per second; I did not use it as a performance figure, only that simulated speeds matched config.
Foot sliding was judged from measured ground speed against the clip speed times playback rate plus visual frames; foot-pixel tracking was not done.
F1 root cause is a hypothesis; the dev should bisect autostep versus the STEP_PROBE path.
decisionsProposed: After the F1 fix, the ramp test should assert peak feet height over the whole run from a start near the ramp for both walk and run, and be mutation-checked.
lessonsProposed: Playwright MCP key presses are instantaneous keydown+keyup, so they cannot hold a movement key against a polled input state; hold keys with a CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent session instead, and read avatar position from the scene (an Object.prototype isScene setter injected via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument captures the scene).

A block-collision test that asserts only the final position can pass while the avatar climbs and steps off: assert the peak over the run, and start near the obstacle, since a far start can hide a near-start failure.
